cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-90592 - Out-of-bounds read in it51xxx I2C target FIFO ISR on oversized read transaction
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-90592
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 9:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 4 minutes ago
Description :The ITE it51xxx I2C driver, when operating as an I2C target (slave) in buffer mode (CONFIG_I2C_TARGET + CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_BUFFER_MODE), transmits response data from the fixed-size data->target_out_buffer inside its target FIFO interrupt handler target_i2c_isr_fifo() in drivers/i2c/i2c_ite_it51xxx.c. On every data interrupt of a host read transaction the handler pushes a fixed 16 bytes from target_out_buffer[i + data->r_index] into the hardware FIFO and then advances data->r_index by 16, without ever checking that index against the size of the buffer. data->r_index is reset to zero only on a STOP or timeout condition, so within a single transaction it only accumulates. An I2C host that keeps clocking read bytes without issuing STOP drives data->r_index past the end of the buffer after sixteen interrupts (default CONFIG_I2C_TARGET_IT51XXX_MAX_BUF_SIZE = 256 bytes), and every interrupt after that reads 16 bytes from beyond target_out_buffer and places them on the bus. What follows the buffer in the driver's device data structure is data->target_shared_fifo and the remaining static device state, so a sufficiently long read transaction streams adjacent firmware memory to the host. The same handler, and the shared-FIFO arm of target_i2c_isr_pio(), also declare the transfer length uninitialised and invoke the optional buf_read_requested() callback without checking that it is registered. A target that supplies no read callback leaves the source pointer NULL and the length indeterminate; when that length compares below the destination size, memcpy() runs with a NULL source. Because the transmit path feeds the FIFO whether or not the callback provided data, such a target also places whatever the previous request left in the buffer onto the bus. The trigger is a malicious or misbehaving I2C master on the same bus (for example a compromised application processor or a rogue device on an exposed I2C bus); no software privilege on the victim is required and the handler runs in the target's kernel/firmware context. The disclosed bytes are not attacker-chosen, but their extent is: the host controls how long the transaction runs and therefore how far past the buffer the driver reads. This is the read-direction counterpart of CVE-2026-14986, which closed the write direction of the same routine without adding the matching bound on the read path.
Severity: 4.6 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-118898 - partisan decodes peer-plane frames with binary_to_term before authentication, allowing a remote VM abort
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-118898
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 4:42 a.m. | 24 minutes ago
Description :Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in lasp-lang partisan allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to abort the Erlang VM of a node via Excessive Allocation. partisan_peer_service_server:handle_info/2 decodes every frame that arrives on the peer listener with binary_to_term/1, without the safe option, before handle_inbound/2 interprets the message and before any peer authentication takes place. TLS is off by default and the listener accepts connections from any host, so one frame that names more atoms than the atom table holds aborts the VM. partisan_peer_service_client:handle_info/2 decodes frames from the server side of a connection the same way. The decode also materializes funs, ports and references the frame encodes and inflates compressed terms. The demonstrated impact is denial of service. partisan does not invoke decoded funs, so code execution was not shown. This issue affects partisan: from 3.0.0 before 6.4.0.
Severity: 8.7 | HIGH

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-59698 - ex_aws normalizes .. in S3 object keys client-side, allowing bucket or key-prefix escape
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-59698
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:45 a.m. | 33 minutes ago
Description :Relative path traversal in ex_aws allows an attacker who controls an S3 object key to escape the intended bucket or key prefix. When ex_aws builds a path-style S3 request, ExAws.Operation.S3.add_bucket_to_path/2 in lib/ex_aws/operation/s3.ex joins the bucket name and the object key into a single path string and then normalizes it, collapsing . and .. segments the way a filesystem path would. Because the bucket is the first segment of the combined string, a leading ../ in the object key pops the bucket off the path. With bucket mybucket and a key of ../victim/secret.txt, the combined /mybucket/../victim/secret.txt normalizes to /victim/secret.txt, so the request (signed with the application's own credentials) is sent to bucket victim. The same mechanism collapses ../ within a key, defeating any isolation an application enforces by prepending a trusted prefix. Only the default path-style configuration is affected; requests built with virtual_host: true do not run this normalization. Because S3 treats object keys as opaque and does not resolve .. itself, the client-side normalization introduces a traversal that would not otherwise exist. Any application that derives an S3 object key from untrusted input and relies on the bucket, or a key prefix, as a tenant or trust boundary is exposed to cross-bucket or cross-prefix read and write, depending on the operation and the credentials' permissions. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.7 before 2.8.0.
Severity: 7.4 | HIGH

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-59697 - IMDSv2 metadata token request follows HTTP redirects in ex_aws
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-59697
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:43 a.m. | 36 minutes ago
Description :Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in ex_aws (instance metadata token provider). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/instance_meta_token_provider.ex and program routines ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.request_token/1 and ExAws.InstanceMetaTokenProvider.get/1. ex_aws requests its IMDSv2 session token from the link-local metadata endpoint (http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) with HTTP redirect following enabled. Because the token request follows 3xx redirects and does not restrict the redirect target to the link-local range, an attacker who can influence the response to the metadata request (for example an on-segment neighbor spoofing the link-local address) can answer with a redirect to an arbitrary host. The library follows the redirect and accepts the arbitrary host's response body as the IMDSv2 session token, caching it and sending it as the x-aws-ec2-metadata-token header on every subsequent metadata and credential request. cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-62269 - S3 object key query-string injection and truncation via unencoded reserved characters in ex_aws
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-62269
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:40 a.m. | 39 minutes ago
Description :Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output vulnerability in ex_aws (S3 request URL construction). This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/ex_aws/request/url.ex and program routines ExAws.Request.Url.build/2, ExAws.Request.Url.sanitize/2 and ExAws.Request.Url.get_path/2. ex_aws does not percent-encode reserved characters in S3 object keys when it assembles the request URL. A literal ? in an object key survives unencoded: build/2 inserts the operation path verbatim and URI.to_string/1 emits it without encoding, and sanitize/2 then splits the flattened URL on the first ?, treating everything after it as the query string. Because the split runs before uri_encode is applied to the path, the ? is never neutralized, and the recovered query is re-inserted without any encoding. An attacker who controls part of an object key (for example a download or upload keyed by a user-supplied filename) can therefore truncate the key past application-appended suffixes, causing the request to address a different object than the application intended, and can inject live S3 sub-resource operations (such as ?acl, ?tagging or ?versions) into the request. The manipulated URL is signed and transmitted normally, so the tampering is authorized like any legitimate request. This issue affects ex_aws: from 2.1.2 before 2.8.0.
Severity: 5.1 | MEDIUM

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-84785 - Unbounded Out-of-Order Fragment Reassembly in QUIC Streams
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-84785
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:30 a.m. | 49 minutes ago
Description :Issue summary: A QUIC peer that sends many small out-of-order STREAM fragments while withholding the first byte of the stream may cause OpenSSL to buffer a large number of reassembly nodes occupying much larger memory than the actual data sent. Impact summary: A remote peer can pin large amounts of memory on a server that accepts incoming QUIC streams, potentially exhausting memory and causing Denial of Service. CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling Description: QUIC receive flow control limits the highest byte offset a peer may reach on a stream. It does not limit how many out-of-order fragments the receiver buffers. OpenSSL allocates a reassembly node for each non-adjacent STREAM fragment and never caps the count. A peer that opens a stream and sends many one-byte fragments at increasing offsets, while withholding the first byte, makes the receiver retain one node per fragment without delivering any data. Only applications that accept incoming streams are exposed. With the default policy, which rejects peer-initiated streams, the stream is torn down before state accumulates. Because the read side never advances past the missing prefix, the flow control window never slides and the nodes stay pinned for the life of the connection. The per-stream window bounds the highest offset, so the memory one stream can pin is finite, but it can reach tens of megabytes and, across many streams and connections, drive memory pressure and Denial of Service. The severity is limited because the exhaustion is bounded by flow control and requires a non-default configuration. FIPS impact: no The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.
Severity: 0.0 | NA

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-96354 - Apache Texera: Missing authorization when adding public projects
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-96354
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 11:17 a.m. | 1 hour, 2 minutes ago
Description :Missing Authorization vulnerability in the public project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating). The public project API did not check that a project had been made public before granting the caller read access to it. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could give themselves lasting read access to other users' private projects and to the private workflows in them, including their version and execution history. Only deployments in which users have created projects are affected; the project feature is hidden in the web UI by default. This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data. If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy. Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project_user_access table, which remains empty unless someone has used the feature: treat any READ grant on a project that is not listed in public_project, and that the project's owner did not give, as suspect. The upgrade deletes this table. Removing a grant does not remove copies the user may already have made of the workflows.
Severity: 0.0 | NA

cvefeed.io Latest.description:

Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 1:24 a.m. | 7 minutes ago
Description :AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.7.1 through 0.8.4, an incomplete IPv6 blocklist in AutoGPT's outbound SSRF protection allows authenticated users to reach local or private network services. Specifically, _is_ip_blocked and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS in autogpt_platform/backend/backend/util/request.py fail to reject the IPv6 unspecified address :: (which connects to ::1 on Linux) as well as 6to4, NAT64, Teredo, and deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 encodings. An attacker can pass :: directly to blocks/sql_query_block.py or blocks/email_block.py, or point URL-fetching blocks, web fetch, MCP servers, webhooks, or OAuth at a hostname whose AAAA record resolves to ::. On backends run directly on a host, this exposes unauthenticated internal RPC services and databases listening on ::1, though the default Docker Compose and single-container deployments bind internal services to IPv4 only. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-136507 - Connection string injection in SQLDriverConnect and the MSDTC XA open string
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136507
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 33 minutes ago
Description :psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early: - In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace. - A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords. - SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed. - On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer. - Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer. An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library. Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
Severity: 8.1 | HIGH
Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-136502 - SQL injection and redirected writes because the driver reads SQL text differently from the server
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136502
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 33 minutes ago
Description :psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table: - An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one. - A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence. - Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted. - A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement. - Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal. - A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table. - An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short. - /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens. - ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time. An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing. Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
Severity: 8.1 | HIGH
Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-136500 - SQL injection with BIG5 aliases and the JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR client encodings
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-136500
Published : Nov. 25, 2026, 11:17 p.m. | 33 minutes ago
Description :To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early. An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only. Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
Severity: 8.1 | HIGH

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-16663 - Pre-authentication out-of-bounds write in MCUboot encrypted serial recovery image decryption
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-16663
Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 5 hours, 14 minutes ago
Description :MCUboot's encrypted serial-recovery path contains an attacker-controlled out-of-bounds stack write in decrypt_region_inplace() in boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c. The routine decrypts an uploaded encrypted image one flash sector at a time into a sector-sized stack VLA buf[sz], but when the current sector is still inside the image header it sets the destination index to the absolute header size (idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size; at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:156) and then decrypts into &buf[idx]. The correct sibling routine boot/bootutil/src/loader.c:876 uses the sector-relative idx = hdr->ih_hdr_size - abs_off; the serial path is missing the - abs_off term, so for any sector after the first the index runs past the end of the stack buffer. The ih_hdr_size field is a uint16_t taken verbatim from the uploaded image header. On the second sector onward, when ih_hdr_size exceeds the sector size, &buf[idx] points beyond buf and boot_enc_decrypt() writes attacker-controlled plaintext into adjacent stack frames. The path is reached pre-authentication: bs_upload() calls boot_handle_enc_fw() (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial.c:1208) after upload, and the pre-decryption signature gate in decrypt_image_inplace() is compiled out (#if 0 at boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:226-233), so the header is never validated before decryption. A second error in the same window computation affects the first sector. When a sector holds both the end of the header and the start of the TLV area, the decrypt length is clamped to tlv_off - (off + bytes_copied), measured from the start of the sector rather than from idx (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c:166). An encrypted image whose header and payload end within the first sector is therefore decrypted for ih_hdr_size bytes more than it should be: into the TLV area and, when the image ends near the end of the sector, past buf. This form needs no oversized header, so even an ordinary small encrypted image can trigger it, and it reaches devices with sectors of up to about 128 KiB rather than only those whose sector is smaller than the 16-bit ih_hdr_size. Reaching the sink requires a build with MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES and serial recovery enabled, and access to the device's serial/USB recovery interface (unauthenticated by design). With the public-key encryption schemes the AES content key is wrapped to the device's public encryption key, so an attacker can author a fully crafted encrypted image — including a malicious ih_hdr_size — without the image-signing private key. The result is a controllable stack memory-corruption inside the bootloader before any signature check, providing a path to code execution in the secure-boot root of trust that bypasses image authentication, as well as a denial-of-service. A 2048-byte out-of-bounds write was reproduced under AddressSanitizer (sz=4096, off=4096, ih_hdr_size=6144). On releases before v2.0.0 (v1.9.0 and v1.10.0) the destination is a file-scope static uint8_t buf[SOC_FLASH_ERASE_BLK_SZ] in .bss rather than the stack VLA described above — the code then lived in boot/zephyr/single_loader.c, before commit c9fa6088 relocated it to boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c and changed the buffer's storage class. The out-of-bounds write is equally real and equally pre-authentication on those releases, but it corrupts adjacent static data rather than the stack, so a stack-smashing proof of concept written against a current release will not reproduce as-is there.
Severity: 8.4 | HIGH

Description :TypesenseVectorStore is vulnerable to a document ID injection in its delete operation that can cause unintended documents to be deleted. TypesenseVectorStore.doDelete(List) builds a Typesense filter_by expression by raw string concatenation of caller-supplied document IDs into the form id: [id1,id2,...] . The Typesense id field uses bare (unquoted) values in this list form with no escaping mechanism. An ID containing characters with syntactic meaning in the Typesense filter grammar — such as a comma ( , ), a closing bracket ( ] ), or operator tokens ( || , && ) — can break out of the list literal and alter the structure of the filter expression. An attacker who controls a document ID passed to the delete operation can use this to delete documents other than the intended ones (comma injection), or to construct a filter that matches every document in the collection (operator breakout), resulting in unintended bulk deletion. Applications that pass externally supplied or user-controlled document IDs to VectorStore.delete(List) backed by TypesenseVectorStore are affected.

Published : Nov. 24, 2026, 6:17 a.m. | 5 hours, 34 minutes ago
Description :Several plugins for WordPress published by WP connect (Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion, WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable, Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms, and Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress) contain embedded malicious code (a backdoor) in the versions listed. The affected releases unconditionally load a backdoor module (includes/airwp-online.php) that runs on every request via the 'init' hook and on a half-hourly WP-Cron event, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress and OS versions, and the server user) to a remote command-and-control server at tascredit-pay.com with TLS certificate verification disabled, and executes the PHP code returned by that server via eval(). The module also accepts queued commands that run shell commands, read, write and delete arbitrary files, query arbitrary database tables, dump the users table including password hashes, drop a webshell into the uploads directory, and install persistent hourly code execution. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers in control of the remote server, or able to intercept its traffic, to execute arbitrary code on the server and fully compromise affected sites. All affected plugins have been closed on WordPress.org and no patched versions are available; we strongly recommend uninstalling them and running a complete malware scan.
Severity: 9.8 | CRITICAL

cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-135055
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 11:17 a.m. | 1 hour, 41 minutes ago
Description :A flaw was found in the GLib DMA-BUF path of WebKitGTK. The UIProcess trusted fds.size() as the DMA-BUF plane count when handling AcceleratedBackingStore::DidCreateDMABufBuffer and copied offsets and strides without verifying that those vectors had the same length. A compromised WebProcess can send mismatched vector lengths, causing an out-of-bounds read in the privileged UIProcess. This can disclose UIProcess memory and crash the UIProcess, and may be used as part of a Web Content sandbox-escape chain.

Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 11:16 a.m. | 1 hour, 41 minutes ago
Description :Synchronet BBS, in versions 3.20b to 3.21e, contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the answer() function when processing the terminal attribute of the SSH service. The call to cryptGetAttributeString() does not limit the copy to the size of the destination buffer, of which 41 bytes are used. An unauthenticated remote client can send a TERM value of up to 64 bytes and overwrite adjacent fields of the session object. If the SSH service is enabled, this tampering can cause connection threads to be blocked for an extended period, even after the client has disconnected. By exhausting the available sockets, the attacker can prevent new connections and cause a denial of service requiring the software to be restarted.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-123886 - Spring Data Elasticsearch SpEL Expression Injection through String-based Query Method Arguments
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-123886
Published : Nov. 23, 2026, 11:16 a.m. | 1 hour, 41 minutes ago
Description :Spring Data Elasticsearch replaces positional placeholders in string-based @Query methods with the method arguments before it evaluates SpEL expressions in the resulting query string. As a result, an argument that contains a SpEL expression is evaluated as part of the query, even if the declared query does not use SpEL. An application is affected if it passes untrusted input as an argument to a repository query method that declares a @Query with positional placeholders. In that case, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary code in the application, and repeated requests can exhaust memory through the unbounded expression cache.
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

Full Disclosure.title: Open WebUI: the Windows installer mints the master key from the install second — CVE-2025-15603 was rejected; here is the measurement
Full Disclosure.description:
Posted by theknell--- via Fulldisclosure on Nov 12

Open WebUI's Windows installer (start_windows.bat) generates
WEBUI_SECRET_KEY — the master secret that signs every session token —
from the C library's rand(), a linear congruential generator seeded
once with the current time in seconds. The key's entire entropy is
the second in which the software was installed.

From any ordinary user's own token, the master key is recoverable
blind in ~2.1 seconds across a ±1-day...

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: BerriAI LiteLLM Guardrail Sandbox Escape RCE
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-40217 is a critical arbitrary-code-execution vulnerability in BerriAI LiteLLM, a widely used open-source LLM proxy/gateway. LiteLLM's guardrail feature includes a "test custom code" facility that runs user-supplied guardrail code in a sandbox. The sandbox can be escaped by rewriting Python bytecode, allowing an attacker to break out and execute arbitrary code in the context of the LiteLLM process (reported running as root in some deployments).

The vector is a request to POST /guardrails/test_custom_code. CVSS is 8.8- the attacker needs minimal low-privilege access, for example a valid API key or low-tier account, so this is not a fully unauthenticated RCE, though that privilege is common in multi-tenant AI gateways. LiteLLM sits at a privileged chokepoint in AI stacks: it brokers model access and stores provider API keys, so code execution there yields those keys and a foothold into the surrounding environment.

Although disclosed on 2026-04-10, the flaw was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog only on 2026-11-18 (remediation due 2026-12-02), after Zenity Labs observed threat actors abusing the guardrail tester to run code as root. A public proof-of-concept and a Nuclei template exist, and EPSS sits around the 99th percentile. LiteLLM also ships bundled inside Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform 2.6, OpenShift AI 3.3, and Lightspeed Core, so organizations may be exposed without having deployed LiteLLM directly.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

• Patch on an emergency basis. Upgrade LiteLLM to the fixed release — confirm the exact fixed version against the vendor / Snyk / Red Hat advisory, as sources list different cut-offs. For bundled products, apply the Red Hat errata RHSA-2026:24866 and RHSA-2026:30056 (Ansible Automation Platform 2.6, OpenShift AI 3.3, Lightspeed Core), and inventory any other product that embeds LiteLLM.
• Reduce exposure now: restrict or disable the guardrail custom-code test feature and the /guardrails/test_custom_code endpoint, and block it at the proxy/WAF if patching must wait. Do not expose the LiteLLM admin/guardrail API to the internet; place it behind authentication and tighten which API keys hold guardrail access (the flaw needs only low privilege).
• Assume compromise for any Internet-reachable or multi-tenant LiteLLM instance left unpatched during the exploitation window. - Rotate all provider/model API keys and any credentials LiteLLM stored or brokered, plus the LiteLLM master key and database credentials.
- Review the host for unexpected child processes, outbound connections, and new accounts.
-Check logs for POST requests to /guardrails/test_custom_code; and watch for abuse of proxied model access (unexpected spend, new model routes).

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is actively monitoring this threat activity and will continue to provide updates, including new intelligence, indicators and protection guidance.
• FortiGuard Intrusion Prevention System: The signature LiteLLM.test_custom_code.Command.Injection (IPS 62918) is available to detect exploit attempts targeting CVE-2026-40217 (https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/ips/62918)
• FortiGuard Antivirus & Behavior Detection: Delivers protection against known malware and uses advanced behavioral analysis to detect and block unknown post-exploitation payloads.
• Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) Service: The FortiGuard team is continuously monitoring for emerging threats and new IOCs.
• FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting a compromise can contact the FortiGuard Incident Response team for rapid investigation and remediation support — API-key theft, model-access abuse, lateral movement.
• Note: network controls do not remediate an application-level compromise of the LiteLLM host; prioritize upgrading LiteLLM and restricting the guardrail test endpoint.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Apache Axis RCE in Confluence Data Center & N-able N-central
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-90436 is a critical unsafe-reflection vulnerability (CWE-470) in Apache Axis 1.x, the legacy SOAP web-services library. Because Axis instantiates classes from attacker-controlled input, an unauthenticated remote attacker can achieve remote code execution on any application that exposes the vulnerable Axis endpoint. The CVSS score is 9.8 (network, low complexity, no privileges, no user interaction). Apache Axis 1.x is end-of-life with no fixed 1.x release, so remediation falls to the products that embed it.

Two widely deployed enterprise products expose the flaw. Atlassian Confluence Data Center (versions 1.x through 9.x) is affected when the Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP) feature is enabled; the exploited endpoint is an unauthenticated POST to /plugins/servlet/soap-axis1/confluenceservice-v2. The feature is off by default for installs created since Confluence 3.0, and Confluence 10.x removed it entirely. Atlassian Cloud is not affected. It is fixed in Confluence 9.2.28. N-able N-central is exposed through its Legacy API feature and is fixed in 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39), released 2026-11-16.

Rapid7 MDR detected in-the-wild exploitation of both products on 2026-11-13, following the 2026-11-06 Apache disclosure (this is an n-day, not a zero-day). A public Metasploit module for Confluence appeared on 2026-11-17, and CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18. Observed post-exploitation has been aggressive and automated: host/network/configuration discovery, database access using Confluence credentials, harvesting of pages and attachments for credentials, tokens, and private keys, an AS-REP roasting attempt against a domain controller, and Microsoft 365 sign-in as an integration service account via legacy authentication. Because N-central is an MSP remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, a single compromise carries supply-chain blast radius across every downstream managed customer.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

• Patch on an emergency basis.
- Confluence Data Center: upgrade to 9.2.28, or to a current 10.x release (10.x removed the vulnerable feature).
- N-able N-central: upgrade to 2026.4 HF3 (2026.4.1.39), and also upgrade Agents and Probes.

• Interim workaround if patching must wait:
- In Confluence, disable Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP) under General Configuration → Further Configuration.
- In N-central, confirm the Legacy API is disabled. These reduce exposure but are not fixes.

• Inventory any other products that embed Apache Axis 1.x (EOL, no fixed 1.x release) and migrate to Axis 2 or apply the embedding vendor's patch.
• Assume compromise for any internet-exposed instance that had the relevant API enabled since ~2026-11-12. Review web logs for unauthenticated POSTs to the Confluence SOAP endpoint and the N-central Legacy API, check for the Confluence/N-central Java process spawning bash or curl, and rotate database credentials, application-link tokens, service-account credentials, and any secrets stored in Confluence pages/attachments.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is actively monitoring this threat activity and will continue to provide updates, including new intelligence, indicators and protection guidance.
•FortiGuard Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): The signature Apache.Axis.CVE-2026-90436.Remote.Code.Execution (IPS 62920) is available to detect exploit attempts targeting CVE-2026-90436. Intrusion Prevention | FortiGuard Labs
• FortiGuard Antivirus & Behavior Detection: Delivers protection against known malware and uses advanced behavioral analysis to detect and block unknown web shells and post-exploitation payloads.
• Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) Service: FortiGuard Labs is continuously monitoring for emerging threats and new IOCs.
• FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting a compromise can contact the FortiGuard Incident Response team for rapid investigation and remediation support.
Note: network controls do not remediate an application-level compromise of Confluence or N-central; prioritize vendor patching and the assume-compromise response.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Armory Castle Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant have disclosed new activity attributed to ARMORY CASTLE (formerly tracked as UNC5221), a suspected China-nexus threat actor primarily targeting VMware vSphere environments. The investigation reveals that the threat actor exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in separate products as part of the same intrusion campaign.

The attackers initially compromised the BeyondTrust appliance, then moved laterally across the internal network, ultimately targeting the VMware infrastructure. They deployed several previously undocumented malware families to establish persistence, steal credentials, compromise vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO), and access ESXi hypervisors and virtual machine data.

- CVE-2026-102764: A zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support, exploited to establish initial access.
- CVE-2026-123890: A VMware vCenter Server vulnerability enabling unauthenticated authentication bypass and ultimately administrative compromise.


One particularly concerning aspect is the ability to steal the vCenter SAML signing key and forge administrative authentication tokens, potentially bypassing MFA and impersonating privileged users.

This demonstrates how compromising centralized virtualization infrastructure can expose multiple virtual machines and the workloads hosted on them. The investigation describes a multi-stage intrusion involving lateral movement, privilege escalation, persistence, credential theft, and ultimately, compromise of the virtualization infrastructure.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations operating VMware vCenter and ESXi should prioritize the following actions:
1. Patch immediately: Apply the official VMware security updates addressing CVE-2026-123890. Also remediate CVE-2026-102764 on affected BeyondTrust deployments.
BT26-05 | BeyondTrust
VMware vCenter Patch

2. Restrict management access: Limit access to vCenter management interfaces, including TCP ports 443, 5480, and 2012, to explicitly authorized systems.
3. Enforce network segmentation: Isolate vCenter and ESXi management interfaces from general corporate networks and other internal appliances.
4. Implement egress filtering: Restrict outbound connections from VMware appliances to prevent unauthorized C2 communications and data exfiltration.
5. Audit privileged accounts: Investigate unexpected SSO administrator accounts, authentication tokens, SSH keys, and changes to vCenter access configurations.
6. Hunt for persistence: Search Linux appliances and VMware systems for the identified malware, webshells, suspicious systemd services, and unauthorized SSH listeners.
7. Review SAML credentials: If compromise is suspected, investigate potential theft of STS signing keys and follow Broadcom's incident response guidance for credential and trust remediation.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiEDR: detects suspicious command execution, privilege escalation, web shell activity, persistence, and malicious processes on supported Linux and endpoint systems.

• FortiGuard Web Filtering: helps restrict access to known malicious infrastructure and suspicious external destinations.
• FortiGuard IoC Service: uses identified network indicators to support threat hunting and blocking through supported integrations.
• FortiNDR: identifies suspicious internal scanning, unusual management-plane communications, and lateral movement.
• FortiPAM: strengthens privileged access controls for administrative accounts and remote access to virtualization infrastructure.
• FortiGuard Incident Response: assists organizations in investigating potential compromise, credential theft, persistence, and data exfiltration.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Java4Shell
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-114938, known as Java4Shell, is a critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Base64 implementation of the Java standard library.

The vulnerability affects Java runtimes on systems using x86-64 processors that support AVX-512 Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions (VBMI). An unauthenticated remote attacker could potentially exploit the flaw by sending specially crafted Base64 data to vulnerable Java processes, resulting in memory corruption, information disclosure, application crashes, or arbitrary code execution.

The vulnerability occurs when the Java Base64 implementation processes specially crafted input using an optimized AVX-512 code path.

An invalid condition in the processing logic can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, potentially corrupting adjacent memory.

Depending on the application and execution environment, successful exploitation could result in:
- Arbitrary code execution within the affected Java process.
- Disclosure of sensitive information from process memory.
- Memory corruption and application crashes.
- Potential compromise of applications and services running vulnerable Java environments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations are advised to review the Oracle Security Alerts for the latest vulnerability details, affected versions, and available patches.

On November 17, 2026, CISA issued an alert urging organizations to immediately patch CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell).

CISA recommends identifying vulnerable Java installations, including runtimes embedded in third-party applications, containers, and appliances, and prioritizing remediation of internet-facing systems. Where patching is not immediately possible, organizations should implement temporary mitigations, including restricting and validating Base64 input and limiting unauthenticated access.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Apache HTTP/2 RCE
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119618 is a race condition (CWE-362) in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module. In assign_headers(), the module writes to a header table that is shared between the connection thread and worker threads without adequate synchronization. Concurrent access can corrupt the Apache child-process heap, which can be leveraged toward remote code execution in the worker process.

Exploitation requires no authentication and no user interaction. The server only reaches the vulnerable code when HTTP/2 is enabled through the Protocols directive (h2 or h2c). The Apache default is HTTP/1.1, which is not exposed.

Apache HTTP Server is one of the most widely deployed web servers, and this flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker over the network on any instance with HTTP/2 enabled.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Affected versions:
• Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, when HTTP/2 is enabled.
• Standalone mod_h2 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.

1. Apply the security update. Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or later, or install the distribution vendor's fixed package, then restart httpd. Prioritize internet-facing servers with HTTP/2 enabled.

2. Confirm exposure. Check whether mod_http2 is loaded (apachectl -M | grep http2) and whether any Protocols directive includes h2 or h2c, globally or per virtual host. Servers without HTTP/2 are not affected.

3. If patching is delayed, set Protocols http/1.1 and check every virtual host. This removes exposure but is not a substitute for patching.

4. Rebuild containers. Rebuild and redeploy container images that bundle the affected Apache versions. Restarting a running container does not update the binary.

5. Standalone mod_h2 users should disable HTTP/2 until a fixed standalone release is available.

6. Monitor for signs of exploitation. Correlate HTTP/2 request bursts with Apache worker crashes, segmentation faults, or restarts. Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by httpd or apache2, and on new files in web roots or temporary directories.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-119618 and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information becomes available.

• FortiGuard IPS has released signature coverage to detect and protect against attacks targeting CVE-2026-119618. IPS Signature 60872

• FortiGuard Vulnerability Management (Endpoint Vulnerability): Released endpoint vulnerability detection that identifies hosts running the affected Apache HTTP Server versions, available in endpoint vulnerability package 2.00814 for Linux. Endpoint Vulnerability | FortiGuard Labs

• FortiGuard Antivirus & Behavior Detection detects and blocks malicious files, web shells, and other payloads that may be delivered or installed following successful exploitation.

• FortiGuard Web Filtering blocks access to known malicious domains, command-and-control infrastructure, and payload-hosting locations associated with post-exploitation activity.

• FortiGuard Indicators of Compromise (IOC) Service can help identify known indicators associated with compromise and malicious infrastructure.

• FortiEDR provides endpoint detection and response capabilities to identify and contain suspicious post-exploitation activity, including unexpected processes and malicious behavior on potentially compromised Apache servers.

• FortiGuard Incident Response supports investigation, containment, and recovery following suspected compromise of affected Apache HTTP Server deployments.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119977 is a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition (CWE-367) in WordPress Core that affects the full-package core upgrade process. During an update, WordPress stages upgrade files in a predictable, web-accessible directory under `wp-content/upgrade/`. These files include the `setup-config.php` installer.

An unauthenticated remote attacker who accesses the staged installer during the upgrade window can exploit this condition to execute arbitrary code on the server. According to published technical analyses, the attacker can supply their own database configuration details, causing the upgrade process to overwrite the site's existing `wp-config.php` file with the attacker's configuration. This can allow the attacker to create an administrator account and execute arbitrary PHP code.

The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 8.1. Exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction but is timing-dependent, as the attack is only possible while a vulnerable site is actively performing a full-package core update.

Although the exploitation window is limited to the duration of the update process, the exposure is significant because WordPress sites are widely deployed and internet-facing. Organizations running affected versions should prioritize applying the security update and verify that no unauthorized changes or administrator accounts were introduced during potentially vulnerable upgrade windows.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Fixed versions: WordPress released 7.1.4 on October 28, 2026, with fixes for each supported branch.

1. Block web access to wp-content/upgrade/ before updating. The first update to a fixed release still runs through the vulnerable updater. Researchers recommend denying the path at the web server (Nginx or Apache) and confirming a 403 response before starting the update.
2. Apply the security update. Upgrade to WordPress 7.1.4, or to the fixed release for your branch, then verify the installed version.
3. Clean up staging files. Delete leftover files under wp-content/upgrade/ that the updater did not remove.
4. Monitor for exploitation attempts. Review web server logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade/, especially setup-config.php.
5. Review for compromise indicators. Check wp-config.php for unexpected changes, such as a different database host. Look for unfamiliar administrator accounts, unknown plugins, and unrecognized PHP files.
6. If compromise is suspected, restore a known-good configuration, rotate database and administrator credentials, and engage incident response.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation of CVE-2026-119977:
- FortiGate Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Provides network-level intrusion prevention and detection against known exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core vulnerabilities. https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/ips/62806
- FortiEDR: Behavioral detection capabilities can help identify suspicious PHP execution, command execution, and other post-exploitation activity on monitored endpoints.
- FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting compromise can engage FortiGuard Incident Response for investigation, containment, and remediation.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: OT Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

November 9, 2026 Update – Threat Attribution: On November 9, 2026, France's CERT-FR published a threat intelligence report attributing the October 11–12 attacks against industrial refrigeration controllers to Shahid Kaveh, an Iranian cyber-offensive unit operating within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Electronic and Cyber Center (IRGC-CEC). According to the report, the attack compromised refrigeration controllers at approximately 700 retail locations across France, modifying defrost settings to trigger high-temperature cycles, resulting in significant product losses and at least 15 reported fires. The assessment is supported by shared attack infrastructure, the use of the FOFA scanning tool, promotion of the operation through the group's CyberbanNews channel, and traces of Persian language in the attack infrastructure. CERT-FR also documents the group's broader targeting of industrial control systems, including Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell equipment, and its historical use of Modbus over TCP port 502 for industrial reconnaissance.

November 2, 2026 Update: A new wave of suspected cyberattacks has affected supermarket refrigeration systems across several European countries, including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia. Reported incidents involved attackers manipulating refrigeration controls and triggering defrost cycles or raising temperatures, with some equipment reportedly reaching 50°C. Affected retailers include ICA, Coop, Carrefour, Delhaize, Colruyt, and SuperValu. Sweden's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-SE) confirmed it was responding to incidents involving ICA and Coop stores. However, authorities have not established whether these incidents are connected to the October attacks in France or share the same threat actors or infrastructure. No threat group has claimed responsibility, and no new malware or indicators of compromise have been publicly confirmed.

On October 11–12, 2026, attackers compromised refrigeration control systems at supermarkets across France, remotely manipulating refrigeration settings and triggering defrost cycles. The attacks caused temperatures in some refrigeration units to rise to as high as 50°C, resulting in food spoilage and operational disruption. Affected retailers reportedly included Intermarché, Netto, Carrefour, Coopérative U, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc.

France's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR, reported compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. These systems monitor and manage commercial refrigeration and related building operations. Their compromise can allow unauthorized changes to operating parameters, potentially disrupting temperature control and damaging perishable goods.

Separate research by Claroty Team82 identified vulnerabilities affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, including:
CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass
CVE-2025-41451, an OS command injection vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution
CVE-2025-41452, a web server configuration vulnerability that can lead to denial of service
Danfoss released fixes for the above vulnerabilities, and organizations should update affected devices to the applicable patched firmware.

Additional research by Claroty Team82 and CISA documented vulnerabilities affecting Copeland XWEB Pro controllers, including:
CVE-2026-25085, an authentication bypass
CVE-2026-21718, an authentication bypass that can enable pre-authentication code execution
CVE-2026-24663, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability
The affected Copeland models include XWEB300D PRO, XWEB500D PRO, and XWEB500B PRO running firmware version 1.12.1 or earlier. Organizations should consult the vendor's remediation guidance and apply the appropriate firmware updates.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

On October 12, France's national cybersecurity response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 warning of numerous compromises involving remote refrigeration controllers.

Organizations should immediately remove direct internet exposure from refrigeration controllers and restrict remote administration to secure VPN connections or protected management networks. Review controller configurations, particularly temperature settings and defrost schedules, and apply available firmware updates and vendor-recommended security settings. Change default credentials and replace unsupported, end-of-life devices where necessary.

If compromise is suspected, isolate affected equipment and follow vendor and CERT-FR recovery guidance before restoring operations. A factory reset alone is insufficient if the device remains vulnerable and exposed. Organizations should also segment OT networks from corporate IT environments, restrict access to authorized personnel, and monitor for unexpected changes to refrigeration settings.

Danfoss identifies firmware R4.2 as the fix for CVE-2025-41450 and R4.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Verify the correct release against the specific device model.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Linux Kernel Remote Code Execution
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-98432, a critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 networking subsystem that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with kernel-level privileges.

The vulnerability stems from improper memory management during TCP connection request processing. Under specific conditions, concurrent operations may access socket-option memory after it has been freed, resulting in a use-after-free condition.

An attacker can potentially trigger this flaw by sending specially crafted IPv4 TCP packets containing IP options to a vulnerable system. Exploitation requires precise timing but does not require authentication or user interaction.

Successful exploitation could result in kernel memory corruption, information disclosure, denial of service, or potentially remote code execution with kernel-level privileges.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerability was introduced in Linux kernel 4.4. The upstream Linux kernel CVE team has published fixes for multiple supported kernel branches.

Ubuntu confirmed on November 2 that fixes for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer were available in its proposed repository while undergoing qualification testing. Ubuntu 26.10 already includes the fix.

Organizations running potentially affected Linux systems should:
1. Apply security updates: Install the latest kernel security updates provided by the respective Linux distribution.
2. Reboot affected systems: Restart systems after installing the updated kernel to ensure the patched kernel is running.
3. Restrict network exposure: Limit unnecessary inbound TCP connections from untrusted networks.
4. Filter IPv4 packets containing IP options: Red Hat provides an interim nftables rule to reduce exposure to the vulnerable code path.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor CVE-2026-98432, including developments in exploitation research, vendor security updates, and the availability of security patches across affected Linux distributions.

• FortiGuard Labs will provide additional updates as new intelligence and protections become available.

The signature provides protection at the network layer, helping prevent exploitation attempts without requiring immediate changes to the underlying Linux kernel. FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Exploitation
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring active exploitation of multiple zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS), an enterprise remote access VPN solution. Threat actors have chained three vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, and CVE-2026-118527) to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on vulnerable appliances.

According to security researchers, the attacks have been observed since at least October 1, 2026. The activity was initially attributed to a previously unidentified threat actor tracked by Volexity as UTA0576.

The attack chain begins with CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute commands without authentication. Attackers then leverage CVE-2026-111357 to escalate privileges and CVE-2026-118527 to upload attacker-controlled files to predetermined locations on the appliance.

Once access is obtained, observed post-exploitation activities include credential theft, Active Directory reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and network scanning. Researchers also reported attempts to retrieve Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) credentials and BitLocker recovery keys.

Notably, the attackers reportedly deployed no malware or web shells. Instead, they re-exploited the appliance to execute individual commands and manipulated system logs to conceal their activity and evade Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool.

Ivanti confirmed that exploitation affected a limited number of customers before disclosure. CISA has now added all three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Ivanti Connect Secure appliances running the following versions are affected:
- Version 25.1.1.2 and earlier.
- Version 25.1.2.2 and earlier.
- Version 22.8R2.5 and earlier.

Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure should immediately apply the latest available security updates.

Recommended actions:
- Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to a fixed release. Versions 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 address the two additional vulnerabilities. Organizations should follow Ivanti's current upgrade guidance for their specific release branch. Do not assume that installing the earlier October update for CVE-2026-104935 provides complete protection. The subsequent vulnerabilities require additional updates.
- Conduct network and memory forensics to identify potential signs of compromise. Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool alone may not identify all exploitation activity.
- If compromise is suspected, follow Ivanti's recovery procedures, including factory resetting affected appliances, rebuilding virtual instances where applicable, and upgrading to a fixed release.
- Reset potentially exposed administrator, domain, and local account passwords. Revoke and reissue stored certificates and reset API keys and other stored credentials.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts involving Ivanti Connect Secure and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation chain:
• FortiGate Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Provides network-level intrusion prevention and detection against known exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-104935. https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/ips/62610
• FortiEDR: Behavioral detection capabilities can help identify suspicious command execution, credential theft, and other post-exploitation activity on monitored endpoints.
• FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting compromise can engage FortiGuard Incident Response for investigation, containment, and remediation.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Node.js Brotli Remote Code Execution (Node2Shell)
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Google Brotli decoder, a component used to decompress data encoded with the Brotli compression algorithm. Brotli is widely used in web communications and is bundled with Node.js through its `zlib` module.

Brotli is an open-source project developed and maintained by Google for lossless data compression. It shrinks files so they can be transmitted faster without affecting the original data.

The vulnerability occurs when the decoder processes specially crafted Brotli-compressed input. An attacker who can supply malicious compressed data to a vulnerable application may corrupt adjacent memory, potentially leading to information disclosure, denial of service, or remote code execution.

The root cause is an error in the decoder's handling of malformed block-switch commands. Under certain conditions, the streaming decoder incorrectly treats an invalid block switch as a request for additional input rather than a format error. This can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, corrupting adjacent process memory.

The vulnerability affects Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. Fixed versions include 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, depending on the release branch. The Node.js project has also released patched versions for affected release lines.

On October 22, 2026, Imperva published research demonstrating remote code execution against a vulnerable Node.js build. Public proof-of-concept references are also listed in Red Hat's vulnerability bulletin, increasing the risk to unpatched deployments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should prioritize updating vulnerable Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries to fixed versions. Because the vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, systems that process untrusted compressed content should receive particular attention.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply security updates: Upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1, as appropriate, or a later fixed release. Update standalone Brotli packages to the applicable fixed version.
2. Review application exposure: Identify services that decompress untrusted Brotli data, including applications using node:zlib, HTTP clients processing compressed responses, and middleware that decompresses incoming request bodies.
3. Apply temporary restrictions where feasible: Until updates are deployed, limit untrusted Brotli-compressed traffic on affected application paths where operationally practical. Test any restrictions to avoid disrupting legitimate traffic.
4. Investigate suspicious activity: Review application and process logs for unexpected crashes or decompression errors. Correlate anomalies with incoming traffic and runtime versions; these symptoms alone do not confirm exploitation.
5. Rebuild and redeploy affected containers: Ensure production images and bundled dependencies include the patched runtime or library rather than relying solely on host-level updates.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-111497 and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information become available. Organizations should prioritize patching affected Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries, particularly where applications process untrusted compressed data.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: PHP2Shell Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP, a widely used server-side scripting language that powers websites and web applications. They involve flaws in PHP's internal request-processing and memory-management behavior that can be triggered when handling malicious requests. Both are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities rated as 9.2 (CVSS 4.0).

• CVE-2026-109618 - RCE via out-of-memory corruption: An out-of-memory condition can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Subsequent request-cleanup operations may incorrectly process this invalid data, potentially enabling remote code execution.

• CVE-2026-109619 - RCE via stale global state: Internal request state can persist after its associated memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may access this stale state before normal initialization resets it, potentially enabling remote code execution.

Successful exploitation could compromise the PHP application process and potentially provide access to sensitive server resources, application data, or databases, depending on the permissions of the affected process and the surrounding environment.

PHP announced emergency security updates for October 21, 2026, following reports that details of the vulnerabilities had leaked ahead of the planned disclosure. Subsequent reports highlighted ongoing exploit research and potential attack activity, underscoring the urgency of applying the available patches. However, widespread exploitation of either vulnerability has not been independently confirmed.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerabilities affect PHP installations that process web requests, including deployments using PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. PHP identifies Apache deployments using mod_php as particularly at risk because a demonstrated exploit can trigger before application code runs.

Organizations should prioritize patching internet-facing PHP servers and other exposed deployments immediately.
1. Apply the security updates. Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, as appropriate. Organizations using vendor-maintained packages should apply the corresponding security updates from their distributions or service providers.
2. Reduce exposure until patching is complete. Where immediate remediation is not possible, isolate affected systems from untrusted networks or temporarily disable exposed services when operationally feasible.
3. Review request-processing limits. Apply appropriate web-server or reverse-proxy limits for request sizes, input fields, multipart sections, headers, and nesting depth. These controls can reduce exposure but are not a substitute for patching.
4. Review potentially vulnerable systems. Investigate suspicious web requests, unexpected PHP worker behavior, unexplained process execution, and unusual access to application files or databases. Prioritize internet-facing systems and investigate potential compromise before returning affected services to production.

PHP 8.1 and older are no longer supported by the PHP project and do not receive its standard security updates. Organizations using these versions should check whether their operating-system vendor provides backported fixes or migrate to a supported release.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs recommends a defense-in-depth approach to reduce exposure to attacks targeting vulnerable PHP deployments and is currently monitoring the situation and will provide updates as new information becomes available and additional protections are released.

• FortiGuard Labs has released IPS signatures to detect and protect against attacks CVE-2026-109619, CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-115560. [IPS version 37.317]

Ubuntu, Debian, and Alpine Linux 3.24 have published fixes. Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.title: Linux kernel RCE CVE-2026-98432
Fortinet PSIRT Advisories.description:
CVSSv3 Score: 9.8

CVE-2026-98432:ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it. Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req(). tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice. Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop() calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed. Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in ip_options_build(). A similar issue exists with request socket migration (net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK, or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree(). Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt (do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well. IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock() duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This will be addressed in a separate patch.

Revised on 2026-11-24 00:00:00
